about.title: Oildale Slip & Fall & Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Oildale sits along the Kern River just north of Bakersfield, home to roughly 36,000 residents who shop, work, and live among a mix of older buildings, rental housing, and commercial strips along North Chester Avenue. When a property owner lets a spill sit uncleaned, ignores broken stairs, or ignores poor lighting in a parking lot, the people who get hurt are often left to sort out medical bills on their own. California law asks whether the owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it — which means what happened in the minutes and hours before your fall can matter as much as the fall itself. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect Oildale residents with independent attorneys who take on these fact-specific claims, working to gather store records, maintenance logs, and any video before it disappears. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Oildale, reaching out costs nothing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can start gathering incident reports and prior complaint history quickly.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and apartment complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting early can mean the difference between having that footage preserved or losing it forever.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to recover a share of damages based on their percentage of responsibility.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Oildale?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your fall happened on public property, such as a Kern County building or sidewalk, that deadline can be much shorter, so it's worth having a claim reviewed as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the store says I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you're found partially responsible — your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help push back on unfair blame-shifting.

items.question: Are older buildings in Oildale treated differently in a premises case?
items.answer: Age of a property doesn't excuse an owner from maintaining safe conditions, but older buildings sometimes come with maintenance records or code history that can support a claim. An independent attorney can help determine what evidence applies to your specific property.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
